# Values content-scan.mjs exempts from a hit because the repository publishes them on purpose.
# One entry per line: an exact string, or a case-insensitive regex wrapped in a leading and
# trailing `/`, matched against the whole matched text (the full email, the full "Bearer ..."
# token, the full number). A human edits this list. Do not add a real customer's address or id
# to work around a failing scan — fix the pattern or the line instead.
#
# Built by scanning every added line of the whole tracked tree (git diff from the empty tree to
# HEAD) with an empty allow-list and classifying every distinct hit. Everything else that
# matched (test fixtures using syntactically valid but fake identifiers, inside the scanner's
# own exempt test directories) needed no entry here at all.

# GitHub's own bot and per-user noreply addresses (committers listed in
# .github/allowed-commit-identities.yml) and its system addresses (action@github.com,
# noreply@github.com, and the "git@github.com:org/repo.git" SSH clone URL, which is
# email-shaped but is not an address).
/@users\.noreply\.github\.com$/
/@github\.com$/

# Claude's fixed commit co-author address (CLAUDE.md's attribution convention), in every commit
# trailer this repository writes.
noreply@anthropic.com

# UK government department contact addresses this repository corresponds with about HMRC MTD
# and Companies House filing (SDSTeam@hmrc.gov.uk, makingtaxdigital-softwarevendors@hmrc.gov.uk,
# xml@companieshouse.gov.uk, noreply@tax.service.gov.uk) and the ICO's own complaints address.
/@[a-z0-9.-]+\.gov\.uk$/
/@([a-z0-9-]+\.)?ico\.org\.uk$/
